assets.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Make one original six-cell educational picture quiz atlas, exact invisible equal 2 rows by 3 columns. Each cell has an independently centered coherent small scene, clear alpha padding of at least 10% on every side, no content shared across cells. Do not add borders, writing, numerals, logos, checkmarks, arrows, panel IDs, lines of text or decorative hints. Match approved clean cut-paper contours, gentle fine paper grain, matte gouache, warm cream, quiet teal and apricot. Keep material, shape, camera angle and scale consistent within each row. The visual relationship carries the answer; avoid color grading or highlights that call one correct option special.
R1C1: overhead of one teal tray with a single clear divider between one wide long compartment and one short compartment, a long cream-handled paintbrush and exactly two short chunky violet crayons lying separately side by side in the long bay, short bay empty. Keep the full tray visible.
R1C2: same teal tray, same angle, same divider and objects. Both short violet crayons lying across and covering most of the long paintbrush in the long bay; a small cream brush end is still visible. Short bay empty.
R1C3: same teal tray, same angle and objects. Long cream-handled brush lying flat alone in the long bay, exactly two short violet crayons visibly separate in the short bay. The divider and all items unmistakable.
R2C1: a quiet original craft desk corner, an ochre open desktop crayon box at a three-quarter overhead view, child hand visibly lifts the one and only cobalt blue crayon out of the box, a few other color crayons remain below in the box. One or two small empty bins in the background if needed for consistency.
R2C2: the same ochre desktop crayon box and same angle. A child hand presses the flat fully opaque ochre lid closed; no crayon outside, no transparent lid, the adjacent small bins in the same places.
R2C3: same desk and small ochre closed crayon box, same other boxes. A child index finger points toward the first closed box without opening it or lifting anything. No crayon outside, no written numbers, no counting marks.
